_format: File system types the entry editor offers. family: local (block device), network, virtual, swap. owner: how file ownership works on the Access tab: mask (uid/gid/umask, for FAT, exFAT and NTFS), cifs (uid/gid/file_mode/dir_mode), posix (files keep their own owners), none. pass: suggested check order for new entries. test: false when the mount sweep can't create this file system (tests/mounttest.cpp).

filesystems.label: ext4
filesystems.description: The standard Linux file system. Reliable, journaled, supports Linux permissions.

filesystems.label: Btrfs
filesystems.description: Linux file system with snapshots, subvolumes, compression and checksums. Kubuntu's default. Btrfs checks itself, so the check order is normally 0.

filesystems.label: XFS
filesystems.description: High-performance journaled Linux file system, good for large files. XFS checks itself while mounting, so the check order is normally 0.

filesystems.label: F2FS
filesystems.description: Linux file system designed for flash storage (SD cards, USB sticks, SSDs).

filesystems.label: ext3 (older)
filesystems.description: Older Linux file system. Handled by the ext4 driver, so the ext4 options apply.

filesystems.label: ext2 (older, no journal)
filesystems.description: Old Linux file system without a journal. Handled by the ext4 driver.

filesystems.label: FAT32 (vfat)
filesystems.description: Windows/DOS file system used on USB sticks, SD cards and EFI partitions. Has no Linux owners or permissions: they are chosen when mounting.

filesystems.label: exFAT
filesystems.description: Microsoft file system for large USB drives and SD cards; files can be larger than 4 GB. Owners and permissions are chosen when mounting.

filesystems.label: NTFS (kernel driver ntfs3)
filesystems.description: Windows' main file system, using the fast in-kernel ntfs3 driver. Owners and permissions are chosen when mounting.

filesystems.label: NTFS (ntfs-3g)
filesystems.description: Windows' main file system, using the ntfs-3g program (mount.ntfs). Slower than ntfs3 but very well tested.

filesystems.label: NTFS (ntfs-3g, explicit)
filesystems.description: Same as 'ntfs' on Kubuntu: always uses the ntfs-3g program.

filesystems.label: UDF (DVD, Blu-ray)
filesystems.description: File system of DVDs, Blu-rays and some external drives.

filesystems.label: ISO 9660 (CD, .iso)
filesystems.description: Read-only file system of CDs and .iso images.

filesystems.label: NFS version 4
filesystems.description: Network share from a Linux/Unix server or NAS (NFS version 4). The device is written as server:/path.

filesystems.label: NFS (any version)
filesystems.description: Network share from a Linux/Unix server or NAS. The version is negotiated, or set with vers=. The device is written as server:/path.

filesystems.label: SMB / Windows share (cifs)
filesystems.description: Windows or Samba network share. The device is written as //server/share.

filesystems.label: SMB 3 only (smb3)
filesystems.description: Like cifs, but only allows SMB version 3 or newer (more secure).

filesystems.label: tmpfs (memory)
filesystems.description: A file system in memory. Fast, and emptied at every restart. The device is usually written as 'tmpfs'.

filesystems.label: Bind mount (folder elsewhere)
filesystems.description: Shows an existing folder at a second place. The device is the existing folder; needs the 'bind' option.

filesystems.label: Swap
filesystems.description: Space on disk the system uses when memory runs low. Has no mount point (written as 'none').

filesystems.label: Detect automatically
filesystems.description: Let mount detect the file system. Only options every file system understands are safe here.
